question: Can I still get a PGWP if I studied part-time in my final semester?
answer: Yes, you can still get a PGWP if you studied part-time in your final semester. The eligibility requirements state that you may study part-time during your final semester. (Source: Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html)

question: I transferred between two designated learning institutions. Can I still get a PGWP if my studies added up to at least 8 months?
answer: Yes, if you transferred between two designated learning institutions (DLIs) and the length of your studies is at least 8 months, you may be eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP). (Source: Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html)

question: Part of my program was an overseas component that earned credit from my Canadian school. Can I still be eligible for a PGWP?
answer: Yes, you may be eligible for a PGWP if your study program has an overseas component that earned credit from a Canadian school. The PGWP will only be valid for the length of the time you studied in Canada. (Source: Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html)

question: While I study in Canada, can I work remotely for an employer outside Canada?
answer: Yes, you can work remotely for an employer outside Canada as long as you still meet the conditions of your study permit. This type of work doesn’t count towards your 24 hours per week off-campus work limit. (Source: Work off campus as an international student, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html)

question: I'm in my last semester and only need a part-time course load. Can I still work off campus?
answer: Yes, you can still work off campus if you are in your last semester and only need a part-time course load. You can work unlimited hours off campus if you meet all the requirements, except the requirement to be a full-time student, and you were a full-time student in your program in Canada until your last semester. (Source: Work off campus as an international student, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html)

question: Can I pay my restoration fees with a credit card that isn't in my name?
answer: Yes, the card you use to pay your restoration fees does not have to be in your name. The cardholder’s name will appear on the receipt but it does not need to match your application. (Source: Extend your study permit or restore your status: How to apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/extend-study-permit/how-to-apply.html)

question: Can my family submit our visitor visa applications together and use one payment receipt?
answer: Yes, families can submit their individual visitor visa applications in one package. The principal applicant must send this combined package to the location where their application will be processed. (Source: Visitor Visa: Applying on paper for specific situations, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/apply-visitor-visa/paper-application.html)

question: I'm a US citizen. Can I fly to Canada without an eTA?
answer: Yes, as a US citizen, you can transit through Canada by air without an eTA. You just need to bring the right travel documents. (Source: Transit through Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/transit.html)

question: My citizenship ceremony is virtual. Can my family watch it in the same room as me?
answer: Yes, your family can watch the virtual citizenship ceremony in the same room as you, but they must not be disruptive and must not join the ceremony on a separate device. (Source: Bringing guests to the ceremony (children, family and friends), https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/become-canadian-citizen/citizenship-ceremony/when.html)

question: My spouse is coming to Canada with me. Can we count money in our joint account as proof of funds for Express Entry?
answer: Yes, you can count money in your joint account as proof of funds for Express Entry. If your spouse is coming with you, you can count money you have together in a joint account. However, you must be able to prove that you have access to the money. (Source: Documents for Express Entry: Proof of funds, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/proof-funds.html)
